cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: `onMessageExternal` is the door open to web pages and other extensions, and this listener hands every message straight to the same privileged command table with no check on `sender.origin` or `sender.id` at all - the TODO above it admits `externally_connectable` has not been narrowed either. Any page that can reach the channel can therefore send `session.token` and walk away with the user's sync token, or `session.describe` for their email, or `session.signOut`.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: The external listener refuses anything that is not a browser-attested trusted sender before dispatching: `sender.id` must be the one companion extension id, or `sender.origin` must be an exact member of the two-entry origin set. Both fields are stamped by the browser rather than taken from the message body, and origin equality cannot be satisfied by a lookalike host or by plain http, so `session.token` is only ever served to the app that is allowed to hold it.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: `route` resolves the handler out of both tables and calls it without ever consulting `senderKind`, even though it computed it one line earlier and the module's own header says workspace commands are meant to be driven from the options page only. A content script runs in every tab and is one page-controlled `postMessage` bridge away from the site it was injected into, so any visited page can reach the workspace-wide commands. The bare table index also resolves inherited keys such as `constructor`, which is why the sibling router uses `Object.hasOwn`.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: Workspace commands are only resolved once the sender has been classified as the extension's own page; a content script or an external sender asking for one gets `forbidden` and the handler is never looked up. Lookups also go through `Object.hasOwn`, so a caller-supplied action cannot resolve to an inherited property of the command table.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: `merge` walks the keys of a JSON document the caller supplied and recurses into `target[key]` with no reserved-key filter. `JSON.parse` produces an own `__proto__` property, so a document shaped like `{"__proto__":{"trusted":true}}` makes the recursion write onto Object.prototype, and every object in the worker inherits the new property. `isTrustedOrigin` a few lines below reads `settings.origins[origin]?.trusted` with no own-property check, so that single patch marks every origin trusted.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: The merge skips `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` before touching `target`, and it only recurses into an existing subtree when that subtree is an own property, replacing it with a fresh object otherwise - so no assignment can reach Object.prototype. `isTrustedOrigin` additionally requires an own property on `settings.origins`, so an inherited key could not be read as a decision even if one existed.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: `note.quote`, `note.author` and `note.sourceTitle` are interpolated raw into an HTML template that is then assigned through `innerHTML` at line 57. The notes are not the extension's own strings: they arrive from the background worker via `sendCommand` in ../shared/messaging, having been captured as page text on whatever site a teammate was reading, so a highlight saved from a hostile page carries markup into every teammate's tab. The shadow root is only a styling boundary - script inside it runs in the page - and this content script can talk to the privileged worker.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: Every stored field is passed through `asText`, which round-trips the value through a text node so `&`, `<` and `>` come back as entities and cannot open a tag in the element content where they are used. The one value that would have had to sit in an attribute, the note id, is written through `dataset` after the markup has been parsed, and the note's CSS class can only be one of two constants from the TONE_CLASS map.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: `payload.url` is an href the content script read out of the page it is rendering, so it is page-controlled, and it is fetched with no parsing, no scheme check and no host restriction from a worker that holds `<all_urls>`. The status and the first 480 characters of the body are handed back to the caller, so a hostile page can use the extension to read `http://localhost` services, cloud metadata endpoints and the customer's internal wiki from inside the reader's network, past the origin policy that would otherwise stop it.

cases.architecture: Chrome MV3 extension: a background service worker with chrome.runtime onMessage/onMessageExternal listeners, a command router, a chrome.storage.sync settings merger, fetch-based preview handlers, and content scripts that render a panel into a shadow root on every page.
cases.why: `previewTarget` parses the value into a real URL first and then requires https, no embedded credentials, and a hostname that is an exact member of the closed PREVIEW_HOSTS set, returning null otherwise; the fetch uses the normalised URL and `redirect: "error"` so an allow-listed host cannot bounce the worker to an internal address. The destination is decided by the extension, not by the page.
